hygiene.meta_title: Dental Cleaning & Hygiene in Montreal | Centre Dentaire du Plateau
hygiene.meta_description: Professional teeth cleaning, scaling and periodontal check-ups on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Personalized prevention for healthy gums and a lasting smile.
hygiene.hero_subtitle: The best dentistry is the kind you never need. Our preventive protocols keep your gums healthy and catch problems before they escalate.
hygiene.description: Healthy gums are the foundation of a beautiful smile and strong teeth. At every periodic check-up, our hygienist removes tartar and plaque that brushing can't reach, assesses your gum health and guides you toward a personalized home hygiene routine. We also screen for gum recession, dentin hypersensitivity, parafunction habits like bruxism, and defective fillings — all conditions that are much easier to address early.
features: Elimination of gum inflammation and periodontal pockets
Detection and correction of traumatic occlusion
Treatment of gum recession and hypersensitivity

faq.q: How often should I get a dental cleaning?
faq.a: For most patients, every 6 months is sufficient. If you tend to accumulate tartar quickly or have a history of gum disease, we recommend every 3 to 4 months.

faq.q: Is scaling painful?
faq.a: Scaling is generally painless. If your gums are sensitive, we can apply a topical anesthetic gel for your comfort before starting.

faq.q: Does my insurance cover dental cleanings?
faq.a: Most dental insurance plans cover 1 to 2 cleanings per year. We help you maximize your coverage at every visit.

faq.q: Are dental cleanings covered by the CDCP?
faq.a: Yes, the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) covers prophylactic cleanings and periodontal assessments for eligible beneficiaries. We submit the claim directly at your visit.

faq.q: How do I know if I have gum disease?
faq.a: The most common signs are gums that bleed when you brush, persistent bad breath, red or swollen gums, and teeth that appear to be 'getting longer' (gum recession). If you notice any of these, book an appointment soon — periodontal disease responds well to treatment when caught early.

veneers.meta_title: Porcelain Veneers & Cosmetic Fillings in Montreal | CDP
veneers.meta_description: Ultra-thin ceramic veneers (0.3 mm) and invisible composite fillings on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Correct colour, shape and gaps with minimal tooth preparation.
veneers.hero_subtitle: Precise, ultra-natural corrections to give you a smile you are proud to show — without compromising the structure of your teeth.
veneers.description: Porcelain veneers are thin ceramic shells (as thin as 0.3 mm) bonded to the visible surface of your teeth to correct colour, shape, mild misalignment or gaps. They require minimal tooth reduction and deliver an exceptionally natural result. Cosmetic composite fillings, meanwhile, replace old grey amalgam restorations and treat cavities invisibly — no one will know the difference. The result is a harmonious smile where the work simply cannot be detected.
features: Correction of colour, shape and diastemas
Natural, long-lasting result (10–15 years for veneers)

faq.q: Do porcelain veneers damage your teeth?
faq.a: Ultra-thin veneers (0.3 mm) require very little — sometimes zero — tooth preparation. They are considered the least invasive option in cosmetic dentistry.

faq.q: How long do veneers last?
faq.a: With proper care (brushing, flossing, regular check-ups), porcelain veneers typically last 10 to 15 years.

faq.q: How many appointments are needed for veneers?
faq.a: Generally 2 to 3 visits: consultation and digital planning, preparation and digital impression, then final placement.

faq.q: Are porcelain veneers covered by dental insurance?
faq.a: Purely cosmetic veneers are generally not covered by insurance. However, if a veneer is replacing a fractured or damaged tooth, partial coverage may apply. We help you check your benefits at the consultation.

faq.q: Can you whiten porcelain veneers?
faq.a: No — ceramic restorations do not respond to whitening agents. If you want a brighter smile, teeth whitening should be done before veneers are placed so the shade of the entire smile can be matched.

rootCanal.meta_title: Root Canal Treatment in Montreal | Crown & Endodontics | CDP
rootCanal.meta_description: Painless root canal therapy at Centre Dentaire du Plateau. Precise endodontic treatment and metal-free ceramic crown to save your natural tooth.
rootCanal.hero_subtitle: Saving your natural tooth is always our first priority. Modern root canal treatment is fast, precise and far more comfortable than you might expect.
rootCanal.description: When the pulp inside a tooth (the living tissue) is infected or irreparably damaged by deep decay or trauma, root canal therapy is the solution to save the tooth without extracting it. We meticulously clean the root canals, disinfect them and seal them hermetically. In the vast majority of cases, a devitalized tooth should then be protected by a metal-free ceramic crown — highly fracture-resistant — which restores its shape and function while preserving aesthetics.
features: Endodontic therapy under local anesthesia — pain-free
Thorough cleaning and hermetic sealing of canals

faq.q: Is a root canal painful?
faq.a: No. Under modern local anesthesia, root canal treatment is no more uncomfortable than a regular filling. It's the pre-existing infection that causes pain — the treatment relieves it.

faq.q: Do I always need a crown after a root canal?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. A devitalized tooth becomes brittle and prone to fracture. A crown protects it and restores its full strength.

faq.q: How long does root canal treatment take?
faq.a: Most treatments are completed in 1 to 2 appointments. Complex cases (curved canals, retreatment) may require 3 sessions.

faq.q: Can I drive or go back to work after a root canal?
faq.a: Yes. The treatment is done under local anesthesia; once it wears off (2 to 3 hours), you can drive and resume normal activities. We recommend avoiding hard foods for the rest of the day.

faq.q: What if my tooth still hurts after the root canal?
faq.a: Mild sensitivity for a few days after treatment is normal. If the discomfort persists beyond a week or intensifies, contact us — it may be residual inflammation or an additional canal that needs attention. A quick follow-up visit resolves it.

implants.meta_title: Dental Implants in Montreal | Plateau Mont-Royal | CDP
implants.meta_description: Dental implant placement on the Plateau Mont-Royal. The permanent, natural-looking solution to replace missing teeth — biocompatible and built to last.
implants.hero_subtitle: A dental implant is the closest thing to a real tooth — beautiful, fully functional and designed to last a lifetime.
implants.description: A dental implant is an artificial root made of biocompatible titanium placed directly into the jawbone. Once osseointegration is complete (3 to 6 months), a custom ceramic crown is attached to the implant to recreate the visible tooth. Unlike bridges, an implant does not require grinding down adjacent teeth. It preserves bone, is cared for just like a natural tooth, and offers results that can last decades. For patients with full or partial dentures, mini-implants can stabilize a removable prosthesis and eliminate unsightly clasps.
features: Implant-supported bridge for multiple missing teeth

faq.q: Am I a candidate for a dental implant?
faq.a: Most healthy adults are candidates. A 3D cone beam scan evaluates available bone volume. In some cases, a bone graft may be needed beforehand.

faq.q: Is implant placement painful?
faq.a: The procedure is performed under local anesthesia and is generally well-tolerated. Post-operative effects are similar to those of an extraction: mild sensitivity and swelling for 48–72 hours.

faq.q: How long does a dental implant last?
faq.a: With proper maintenance (brushing, flossing, annual check-ups), an implant can last 20 to 30 years — often a lifetime.

faq.q: How much does a dental implant cost in Montreal?
faq.a: The cost of an implant varies by clinical situation, but typically ranges from $2,500 to $4,500 for the implant and crown combined. A consultation with a 3D radiographic assessment is needed for a precise quote. We also help you determine whether your insurance or the CDCP can cover part of the cost.

faq.q: Are dental implants covered by the CDCP?
faq.a: The CDCP covers certain surgical acts related to implants depending on your coverage tier and clinical situation. At your consultation, we verify your eligibility and submit the claim on your behalf.

orthodontics.meta_title: Invisalign Montreal | Invisible Orthodontics for Adults & Teens | CDP
orthodontics.meta_description: Straighten your teeth discreetly with Invisalign on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Metal-free orthodontics for adults and teenagers. Free Invisalign consultation.
orthodontics.hero_subtitle: Align your teeth without brackets, without metal, without aesthetic compromise — at your pace, with custom clear aligners.
orthodontics.description: Invisalign® is the world's most advanced invisible orthodontic system. Each series of clear aligners is custom-made from a digital impression (Trios 3D scanner) and progressively moves your teeth toward the computer-planned target position. The aligners are removable — take them out to eat and brush your teeth — and virtually invisible, making them ideal for adults and teens who care about their appearance. We show you a virtual preview of your final smile before treatment even begins.
features: Invisalign® clear aligners — discreet and comfortable
3D digital planning with final smile preview

faq.q: How long does Invisalign treatment take?
faq.a: A mild case can be completed in 6 to 12 months. More complex cases take 18 to 24 months. The exact duration is determined at your initial consultation.

faq.q: Is Invisalign as effective as traditional braces?
faq.a: For the majority of cases, yes. Invisalign effectively treats moderate crowding, gaps and mild to moderate malocclusion. Very severe cases may still require braces.

faq.q: How much does Invisalign cost?
faq.a: Costs vary by case complexity (approximately $3,500 to $7,000). We offer an initial consultation to assess your case and provide an accurate quote.

faq.q: Does insurance cover Invisalign?
faq.a: Some dental insurance plans include partial orthodontic coverage (braces or Invisalign), often between $1,000 and $2,500 lifetime maximum. We help you maximize your benefits at the consultation.

faq.q: Do I need retainers after Invisalign?
faq.a: Yes — retainers are essential to maintain your results. We custom-fabricate them at the end of your treatment. Worn at night, they keep your teeth in their new position long-term.

surgery.meta_title: Oral Surgery in Montreal | Tooth Extraction & Gum Graft | CDP
surgery.meta_description: Tooth extractions, gum grafts and implant surgery on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Precise, gentle surgical care for fast recovery.
surgery.hero_subtitle: When surgery is needed, our minimally invasive techniques and careful approach ensure your comfort and a smooth, speedy recovery.
surgery.description: Our oral surgery services cover the extraction of severely compromised or highly mobile teeth (in advanced periodontal disease), implant placement, and gum grafts to treat recession or congenital absence of attached gingiva. All procedures are performed under local anesthesia using minimally invasive techniques and, where possible, assisted by our Bluewave laser to reduce bleeding and accelerate healing.
features: Extraction of severely damaged or fractured teeth
Extraction of highly mobile teeth (periodontal disease)
Gum graft (recession or congenital absence of gingiva)
Treatment of root hypersensitivity through tissue grafting
Bluewave laser assistance for reduced bleeding

faq.q: Are tooth extractions painful?
faq.a: Extractions are performed under local anesthesia and should not be painful during the procedure. Post-operative discomfort (24–48h) is managed with standard pain relievers.

faq.q: What is a gum graft?
faq.a: It is a procedure where gingival tissue (taken from the palate or a tissue bank) is grafted onto a recession area to cover the exposed root and prevent sensitivity and bone loss.

faq.q: How long is recovery after oral surgery?
faq.a: For a simple extraction, 24–48 hours. For a gum graft or implant placement, expect 3 to 7 days before returning to normal activity.

faq.q: Can I eat normally after a tooth extraction?
faq.a: Avoid hard, hot foods and straws for the first 24 hours to protect the blood clot. Stick to soft foods (soups, yogurt, mashed potatoes). You can generally resume normal eating after 48 to 72 hours.

faq.q: Is a gum graft painful?
faq.a: The procedure is performed under local anesthesia and is not painful during surgery. Mild to moderate post-operative discomfort (palate tenderness, slight swelling) is common for 3 to 5 days and is managed with standard pain relievers.

radiology.meta_title: Digital Dental X-Ray Montreal | Panoramic & Cone Beam | CDP
radiology.meta_description: 100% digital dental radiology on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Planmeca panoramic, intraoral sensors and 3D cone beam for precise diagnostics with minimal radiation.
radiology.hero_subtitle: Sharper images, more accurate diagnoses, and up to 90% less radiation than conventional equipment — for your health and the environment.
radiology.description: Digital radiology is at the heart of our diagnostic approach. Our Planmeca panoramic unit and digital intraoral sensors produce high-resolution images instantly available on screen — no developing time, no chemicals. Radiation dose is reduced by up to 90% compared to analogue equipment. For implant planning or complex case evaluation, our 3D cone beam provides a complete three-dimensional view of bone and dental structures.
features: 3D cone beam imaging for implant planning
Up to 90% less radiation vs analogue

faq.q: Are dental X-rays dangerous?
faq.a: With our digital technology, the radiation dose is extremely low — comparable to a few hours of cosmic radiation during a flight. The diagnostic benefits far outweigh the risk.

faq.q: How often should I have dental X-rays?
faq.a: For a healthy adult with no risk factors: a panoramic X-ray every 3–5 years and bitewing X-rays every 1–2 years during routine exams.

faq.q: What is a cone beam CT scan?
faq.a: It is a dental scanner that produces a full 3D reconstruction of your jaws and teeth. Essential for precisely planning implant placement or evaluating complex cases.

faq.q: Are dental X-rays covered by insurance?
faq.a: Yes — diagnostic X-rays (bitewings, panoramic) are generally covered by dental insurance plans at defined intervals (e.g., bitewings every 1–2 years). We submit the claim directly to your insurer.

faq.q: Can pregnant women have dental X-rays?
faq.a: With our digital technology, the radiation dose is extremely low. When clinically necessary (pain, infection), X-rays can be taken with a lead apron for protection. We recommend postponing routine X-rays to the second trimester or after delivery whenever possible.

whitening.meta_title: Professional Teeth Whitening Montreal | Plateau | CDP
whitening.meta_description: Professional teeth whitening at Centre Dentaire du Plateau. Visible, lasting results with minimal sensitivity. Achieve a brighter smile safely.
whitening.hero_subtitle: A smile several shades brighter in one session — with safe, dentist-supervised products that deliver results that last.
whitening.description: Professional teeth whitening is the safest and most effective way to brighten your smile. Unlike over-the-counter kits, our protocols use optimal-concentration whitening agents tailored to your teeth and applied under dental supervision. We offer two formats: in-office whitening (immediate results in one hour) and take-home whitening with custom-fitted trays (for a gradual treatment at your own pace). Both options can be combined for maximum impact.
features: Visible results of 4 to 8 shades lighter
Post-treatment fluoride protocol for lasting brightness

faq.q: Is teeth whitening safe?
faq.a: Yes, when performed under dental supervision with appropriate products. We first assess your gum health and enamel condition to tailor the protocol to your situation.

faq.q: How long do whitening results last?
faq.a: On average 1 to 3 years depending on your dietary habits (coffee, tea, red wine, tobacco). Occasional touch-ups with the custom trays help maintain brightness.

faq.q: Does whitening work on crowns and veneers?
faq.a: No — ceramic and composite restorations do not respond to whitening agents. We plan the treatment to harmonize the overall shade of your smile.

faq.q: Is professional teeth whitening covered by insurance?
faq.a: No — teeth whitening is considered a cosmetic procedure and is not covered by standard dental insurance. That said, the results of a professional whitening are significantly superior to over-the-counter kits, often at a comparable price point.

faq.q: At what age can you start teeth whitening?
faq.a: We recommend waiting until all adult teeth have fully erupted, generally from age 16 to 18. Before that age, enamel is still developing and whitening is not advisable.

technology.meta_title: Advanced Dental Technology Montreal | 3D Scanner, Laser | CDP
technology.meta_description: Trios 3D oral scanner, Bluewave diode laser and full digital radiology at Centre Dentaire du Plateau. Technology in service of more precise and comfortable care.
technology.hero_title: Advanced Technology in Service of Your Smile
technology.hero_subtitle: We continuously invest in the latest innovations so that every treatment is more accurate, faster and more comfortable for you.
technology.description: Modern technology is radically transforming the dental experience. Our Trios oral scanner (3Shape) replaces unpleasant impression pastes with a digital scan in seconds — more precise and instantly transmittable to the laboratory. Our Bluewave diode laser treats soft tissue (gums) without bleeding, without sutures in most cases, and accelerates healing. Our fully digital radiology (panoramic + intraoral sensors + 3D cone beam) reduces radiation exposure and improves diagnostic quality. Together, these technologies enable less invasive, more predictable care and consistently high-quality results.
features: Trios 3D oral scanner — digital impressions, no paste
Bluewave diode laser for soft tissue (no scalpel)
3D cone beam imaging for implant surgery

faq.q: What is a Trios oral scanner?
faq.a: It is a device that captures a 3D digital impression of your teeth in minutes — no paste, no discomfort. The data is sent directly to the dental lab to fabricate crowns, veneers and aligners with sub-millimetre precision.

faq.q: Does the dental laser replace the drill?
faq.a: The Bluewave diode laser is used specifically for soft tissue (gums). It does not replace the drill for cavity treatment, but it allows gum procedures (reshaping, periodontal treatment) without a scalpel and with less post-operative discomfort.

faq.q: Do these technologies increase the cost of care?
faq.a: Some technologies carry a slightly higher cost (e.g. digital vs conventional impression), but they often reduce the number of appointments needed and improve precision, which avoids costly remakes.

faq.q: Is a digital impression (Trios scanner) more accurate than a traditional one?
faq.a: Yes — digital impressions have sub-millimetre accuracy, eliminate distortions from impression paste, and are transmitted instantly to the lab. This means better-fitting crowns, veneers and aligners, and fewer adjustment appointments.

faq.q: What is Digital Smile Design (DSD)?
faq.a: Digital Smile Design is a planning software that simulates your final smile on screen before any treatment begins. It lets you visualize the expected result for veneers, implants or orthodontic work, and helps us design a smile that fits your face and preferences.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before your visit.

new_patients.question: First visit or new to Canada?
new_patients.answer: We warmly welcome new patients and people who have recently arrived in Canada. During your first visit, we perform a complete oral health assessment (clinical exam + X-rays) to establish your personalized treatment plan. Our multilingual team guides you through all administrative steps: enrolling in insurance, using the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP), and understanding your coverage. You don't need to prepare anything — we take care of everything.

cdcp.question: Do you accept the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP)?
cdcp.answer: Yes, we are a CDCP partner. This federal program is open to all Canadian residents without private dental insurance whose family net income is under $90,000/year. It covers a wide range of services: exams, cleanings, fillings, crowns, root canals, extractions and more. To benefit, register at canada.ca, then present your membership card at your appointment — we submit the claim directly. Coverage renews annually after you file your income tax return.

payment.question: What are your payment methods?
payment.answer: We accept credit cards, checks, and cash. We also work with most insurance providers for direct billing.

emergency.question: How to handle a weekend emergency?
emergency.answer: On Sundays, we are open from 10am to 2pm for urgent care. Outside these hours, please contact the on-call service.

languages.question: Do you speak other languages?
languages.answer: Yes, our team communicates in French, English, and Tagalog. We make sure every patient fully understands their treatment plan, regardless of language.

insurance_direct.question: Can you bill my insurance directly?
insurance_direct.answer: Yes, we offer direct billing with most private insurance providers. Just bring your insurance card to your appointment and we handle the submission — you only pay the portion not covered by your plan.

children.question: Do you accept children?
children.answer: Absolutely — we treat patients of all ages, from toddlers to seniors. Our dentists are experienced in making children feel comfortable and explaining procedures in a fun, engaging way to build healthy habits from an early age.

ramq.question: Does the RAMQ cover dental care?
ramq.answer: The RAMQ covers basic dental care for children under 10 (exams, cleanings, fillings, extractions). For adults, the RAMQ generally does not cover dental care, except in rare cases such as certain oral surgeries performed in a hospital setting. If you have no private insurance, the federal Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) may cover a large portion of your costs — we are a registered CDCP provider.
